I’m currently studying public health at Appalachian State University, where I’ve gained a deep understanding of the field and developed a real passion for it. I’ve particularly enjoyed working with data and I have found the process of analyzing health trends fascinating — my biostatistics class really highlighted how powerful data analysis can be in addressing public health issues. Through my extracurricular and research experiences, I’ve learned about the many different aspects of public health and have become even more motivated to dive deeper into this field. I’m especially interested in areas like disease prevention, health behavior theory, and reducing health disparities. As I continue my studies, I’m excited to use my knowledge and skills to make a positive impact in these areas.

Through my coursework and hands-on experience, I've developed a strong foundation in public health research, data analysis, and community service. Below are some of the highlights of my academic and professional journey:

**Departmental Honors Program: Thesis & Honors Coursework**

I have been working on a research project regarding tick-borne illness among long-distance Appalachian Trail hikers. Throughout this experience, I have learned the process of conducting academic research from the ground up. I have created a partnership with the Appalachian Trail Conservancy, developed skills in technical writing, and I am looking forward to start collecting and analyzing data in May 2025. The departmental honors program has also given me the opportunity to take classes for honors credit and gain a deeper understanding of my coursework.

**Public Health Americorps Fellowship: Evaluation Team**
  
As a Public Health Americorps fellow, I am collaborating with a dedicated team of public health students and professionals to address critical mental health needs in Western North Carolina, focusing on strengthening community resilience through evidence-based interventions like Psychological First Aid. On the Evaluation Team, I will be applying my skills in data collection and analysis to assess the effectiveness of these interventions and ensure their impact aligns with community needs.

**Undergraduate Research Assistantship: Eco-Anxiety Analysis**
  
As a Research Assistant at Appalachian State University's Research Institute for Environment, Energy, and Economics, I collaborated with a team to analyze crisis text conversations, focusing on themes of eco-anxiety and climate worry. Through thematic analysis, I contributed to identifying and interpreting patterns in these critical discussions, providing insights into the mental health impacts of environmental concerns. This work culminated in a research paper titled "Eco-Anxiety, Climate Concern, and Fatalistic Outlooks: Insights from U.S. Crisis Text Conversations on Climate Distress" which is currently available as a preprint on Preprints with The Lancet.
